findings.title: Support's confirmation names the masked killer the picker drew as "?": a bystander or the victim learns who the killer is for the price of opening a window
findings.where: scripts/calls.mjs:721 (`const aimed = describeChoice(choice)`), 769-770 (the "Aimed at" line), 878-880 (`describeChoice` answers `choice.target.name`); scripts/call-pickers.mjs:430-433 (the picker draws `nameAsSeen(a)` and hands back the actor itself); scripts/sheet-actions.mjs:908-909, 929 (the picker's choice handed to confirmCall); scripts/mask-gm.mjs:148-158 (`nameAsSeen`)
findings.what_happens: pickPlayer lists the people in the buyer's room by nameAsSeen, so a masked killer reads "?" to another player (owner-115 item 1b). The row's value is the actor id, and pickPlayer answers `{ target: <the actor> }`. runCall then opens confirmCall with that choice, and confirmCall prints `Aimed at: ${describeChoice(choice)}`, which is `choice.target.name` - the actor's real name, drawn in a window on the buyer's own browser. No card is involved, so secret.mjs's mask cut (`wordsFor`, which writes names hidden from a reader as "?" on private cards) never reaches it. Cancel costs nothing; the sheet asks only that the buyer holds Support's 1 Hope before the picker (sheet-actions.mjs:865-871).
findings.failure_scenario: A direct murder opens on Hope and the killer stands behind a "?"; the victim (or a third student in the room) presses Support, picks the "?" row, reads "Aimed at: Chie Mori" in the confirmation and presses Cancel, having paid nothing.
findings.expected: The confirmation names the target as the picker did (nameAsSeen), so a masked character reads "?" there too; docs/dev/owner-115/STATUS.md item 1: while the mask stands the killer's identity is secret from everyone not in on it.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a mask guard on the road: callBarred and hopeCallRefusal ask only the Eclipse, the Silence weather, death and the Silence Call (calls.mjs:64-130; allowed-now.mjs:92 shuts callHope only in an Eclipse), so a Support may be bought during and after the fight; pickPlayer reads othersInRoom (movement.mjs:3781-3785, token documents) and studentActors, both of which hold the masked killer; nothing in runCall rewrites `choice` between the picker and confirmCall (sheet-actions.mjs:908-929). The receipt and the beneficiary's notice are private cards and are cut by wordsFor, so they are not part of this finding. R7404 (tests-tier1.mjs:59209) reads call-pickers.mjs's picker source for nameAsSeen and does not read calls.mjs's confirmation; no test reads `describeChoice` (grep of scripts/tests*.mjs and audit/harness/scenarios for aimedAt and describeChoice: none). The base run was not available, so R7404's result was not read.
findings.tests_near: R7404 (scripts/tests-tier1.mjs:59209), the six pickers' source; scenario 21's masked fight reads cards and the scan, not a Call window.
findings.live_check: new live check: with a mask standing after a direct murder opened on Hope, on the victim's browser press Support, pick "?" and read the confirmation's "Aimed at" line; it should say "?".

findings.title: A Despair Call aimed at a masked killer names them on the public card to every player
findings.where: scripts/calls.mjs:525-534 (the public card, `announce` with no whisper list); scripts/call-effects.mjs:1000-1003 (Obstacle and Approval: `name: beneficiary.name`), 1044-1046 (Despair as Hope), 1099-1102 (Pain, Paranoia), 1288 (Silence), 1303 (Chained); scripts/utils.mjs:701-716 and 815-831 (a card with no whisper list is `ChatMessage.create` with the content as written); scripts/secret.mjs:496-499 (the mask cut lives in `wordsFor`, which only private cards pass)
findings.what_happens: spendDespairCallFor posts the Call's public card with the effect's receipt lines, and every Call aimed at a student writes that student's real name into a line ("{name}'s next roll gets {what}.", "{name} loses {what}.", "{name} cannot spend Hope Calls ...", "{name} is chained ..."). A public card goes to `ChatMessage.create` with its words in the document (utils.mjs privately, no recipients), so the mask's cut, which secret.mjs applies to each reader's copy of a private card's words, is never asked. The GM's picker lists real names, so nothing on the GM's side marks the masked character either.
findings.failure_scenario: While the killer stands behind a "?", the Monokuma's GM buys Pain on the student it knows to be the killer; every player's chat shows "Pain - Chie Mori loses 2 Health", and the table knows who the "?" is.
findings.expected: While a mask stands, a public card names a masked character as "?" to non-insiders, as the crisis card does (murder-rules.mjs `maskedName`, owner-115 item 1), or the Despair Call's lines go through the same cut.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another cut of public cards: grep for maskNames and namesHiddenFrom outside mask-gm.mjs finds secret.mjs (private cards) and frisk.mjs (its own packet) only; no renderChatMessage hook rewrites a public card's names. spendDespairCallFor has no mask question (calls.mjs:408-554). The design says Despair Calls are public (calls.mjs:13-14, 507-518) and the chain's room was taken off the card for privacy (call-effects.mjs:1301-1303), so the name on the card is the rule; what is not covered is the mask's period, which the owner's rule of 14.11 makes secret from everyone not in on it. It needs a GM to aim a Call at the masked character, so it is major rather than a blocker.

findings.title: A co-owner's own call on the GM (Search for something specific, Observe, Analyze, a project proposal, a Tier 0 item's use) goes to the other owner's thread
findings.where: scripts/call-gm.mjs:951 (`threadOf(actor, thread)`), 1018-1022 (`threadOf` falls back to `ownerOf` with no `thread`); scripts/utils.mjs:642-647 (`ownerOf`: the first active non-GM owner); callers on the roller's browser with no `thread`: scripts/action-search.mjs:148, scripts/action-observe.mjs:232, scripts/action-analyze.mjs:259, scripts/action-project.mjs:416, scripts/call-gm.mjs:1306 (promptAndCallGm, used by use-items.mjs:596)
findings.what_happens: E18 fix e1-G7 sends a card to its asker's thread only for the asks the primary holds (Call, Dynamic, statistic, Observe's gaze), which pass `thread: ctx.asker`. Every card a player's own browser posts through callGm passes no `thread`, so threadOf answers ownerOf(actor): the first connected player owner. When a second player owns the character too, that player's request lands in the first owner's thread, whispered to that player and the GMs only (messenger.mjs:276), and since E91 C6 the GM's ruling follows the card into that thread. The asker reads nothing in their own thread.
findings.failure_scenario: Two players share Aiko; the second rolls Search for something specific and writes what they look for: the card, its 'Open until' and the GM's answer go to the first player's GM Chat, and the second waits on a thread that never shows it.
findings.expected: A card a player's own browser posts goes to that player's thread when they own the character (`thread: game.user.id`), as the comment at call-gm.mjs:1009-1016 states for the primary's asks.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether callGm defaults `thread` to the poster: it defaults to null (call-gm.mjs:923). Checked the tier 2 test 'a co-owner's question lands in the co-owner's thread' (tests-tier2.mjs:39773-39836): it drives `dynamic.difficulty` through the bridge's runner, the primary-held road, and reads nothing of the local roads. Co-owned characters are a supported case (utils.mjs:649-651 playerOwns, E91 C6, D078), so the situation exists; it is rare, hence minor.

findings.title: A refused or unanswered arm of a Hope Call says so twice, and logs an error for an ordinary refusal
findings.where: scripts/calls.mjs:303-308 (`notArmedNotCharged` after `failed && gmPays`); scripts/call-effects.mjs:283-288 (armCall answers null on the bridge's refusal), 990-997 (grantEffect throws an Error), 1405-1415 (applyCall logs it with `error(...)`); scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:466-477 (requestArmCall, through `ask`, which says the refusal); .claude/rules/trust-model.md 'How to add a bridge action' step 4
findings.what_happens: Since E29 C8 every Hope Call that grants a roll is armed on the primary. When the GM side refuses it, or no GM answers, the bridge's `ask` says "... was not carried out: <why>" (sayNotDone), armCall answers null, grantEffect throws a plain Error, applyCall writes 'Could not fully apply' at error level, and spendHopeCall then warns "{call} was not armed. You keep your Hope." - two notices for one refusal, the second from the caller, which the rule says never shows its own refused message.
findings.failure_scenario: A player buys a Loaded Die while the GM's browser holds one already armed: a toast says the arm was not carried out because it is already held, a second says the Loaded Die was not armed and the Hope is kept, and the GM's diagnostics count an error.
findings.expected: One notice (the bridge's, which can say nothing was spent), and a refusal that is not a fault kept out of the error log, as DESP-19 settled for the refund road.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether the bridge stays quiet on call.arm: the row has no `quiet` and no `tell` (bridge-table.mjs:932-970) and requestArmCall passes no `quiet` (bridge-asks.mjs:466-477), so its refusal is said. The sheet's own pre-check (sheet-actions.mjs:899-905) catches a second copy for a Call with no target before the price, so the double needs a GM-side refusal the sheet did not foresee or a GM that does not answer. Related to DESP-19 (fixed for the refund road), not the same road.

findings.title: Two GMs writing a seal or a restriction at once keep only one: the sealed rooms and the restrictions are read and written whole from each GM's copy
findings.where: scripts/call-world.mjs:65-69 (sealRoom), 134-139 (restrict), 202-207 (writeWorld); compare scripts/despair.mjs:330-349 (the pools' one writer and serialWrite, DESP-12)
findings.what_happens: sealRoom and restrict read the world setting on this GM's browser, add one entry and set the whole value. Two Monokumas on two GM browsers buying Silence on two students (or two Seals) within one round trip each read the old value, and the second write drops the first's entry - both paid, both public cards say it landed. restrict also answers true whatever writeWorld answered, where sealRoomEffect checks the write (call-effects.mjs:1275-1277), so a Silence or a Chain is announced even when nothing was written.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs, each with a Monokuma, Silence Aiko and Botan in the same second: both cards say silenced, both pools pay 4, and only Botan is silenced.
findings.expected: One writer for these two settings, as DESP-12 gave the pools (the primary, or a serial step), and restrict's answer the write's.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a serial step or a primary hand-off around writeWorld: none (call-world.mjs:202-207); Despair Calls are bought on any GM's browser (calls.mjs:416-419 refuses only players). The interleaving itself was not measured; it needs two GMs within network latency, so minor.

findings.title: A note or a new rule that reads "cancel" is taken for the Cancel button
findings.where: scripts/calls.mjs:788-791 and 804 (confirmCall: the callback answers the note bare, `result === "cancel"` returns null); scripts/call-pickers.mjs:326 and 330 (pickText: the rule's words bare, `text === "cancel"`); compare scripts/call-gm.mjs:1208-1211 and 1239 (askForRequest answers `{ text }` since E18 C0, S10-52)
findings.what_happens: The two windows answer the typed words themselves, and the kit's Cancel answers its action "cancel", so the words "cancel" (or "Cancel" after no case change - only the exact lower-case word) are read as Cancel: an Experience's note "cancel" closes with nothing sent and nothing said, and a New Rule "cancel" is dropped. askForRequest fixed the same shape in E18 C0.

findings.refutation_tried: Talent's rows answer an object, so only the bare-note Calls and pickText are touched; choose() answers ids and room names, where a room named "cancel" is the same shape but unlikely.

l1.what: an ask card left open across a primary GM's reload ends at its time
recipe: 2. The player asks a Dynamic action; the card goes up with 'Open until'.
3. The GM reloads before answering and does not touch the card.
4. Wait past the card's time plus a few seconds.
5. Read the card on both browsers.

l1.what: two GMs silencing two students at once keep both silences

3. Press Spend on both within a second.

recipe: 1. One GM, three players: killer, victim, bystander in one room.
2. A direct murder whose opening succeeds on Hope, so the killer's token reads '?'.
3. On the victim's browser: Support, pick '?', read 'Aimed at', Cancel.
4. On the GM: a Despair Call (Obstacle) on the killer; read the public card on the bystander's browser.
l1.settles_if: '?' in both places (fixed) / the killer's name in either (the finding stands)
